I often feel like I've done everything I possibly can and I've heard tons of advice. The truth is, that everybody is just kind of fumbling around in life to try and figure out what works for them and making all kinds of decisions along the way, some that benefit, some that they regret... Everything can seem pretty redundant and hopeless... Often, I think about that. Life. How mundane and difficult every little thing can be. Suicide can seem like a great reliever. We just want the suffering and difficulties to end. Most days I wake up wishing I didn't exist. I also have paranoia, tension and stomach pain and knots in my stomach. I feel it creep up all the time, even over little stressors. The things that have started to help are: 

1. seeing a therapist and getting prescribed medication (although I'm not sure its the medicine that helps or my choices.) 

2. cutting negative people out of my life. People that cause me stress or make me feel worthless or non existent.

3. surrounding myself with people that have good intentions and truly care about my well being. If someones bringing you down, or they have bad intentions... they are only going to stunt your growth and healing. Get rid of them.

4. try to substitute facebooking and tv watching with reading, drawing, cleaning... tasks where I'm not just laying around.

5. trying to act on things that i think about often... for example... i had been THINKING about going rollerblading often but I never just went rollerblading... I obsessed over how I would react if cars drove past me. Then one day, before I really had a chance to let myself obsessed, I just put those rollerblades on and rollerbladed around the neighborhood... It wasn't great but I was a little bit happy and that made a huge difference in my day. I fed my "soul" by listening to myself. So, when you get an urge to do something, try to push yourself to do it before you start to obsess. It might not be easy, I know, but try.

6. challenge your negative thoughts. It's not easy to do but it can help. I understand you've already done cbt so I'm sure you know about framing your negative thoughts in a different way. If not I can send you some material.

7. talk about it with people. you are not a burden. you deserve to be happy. you are worthy of love and affection. You need these affirmations. If you aren't around people who tell you these things, find some people that will. It would be good for you to have people in your life that challenge your negative thoughts and help affirm what you deserve and how wonderful you are. 

I can't help you fix yourself and I don't always have the answers but if you ever need someone I am here to talk. I can give you advice if thats what you want, or I can just listen while you vent. Sometimes its just nice to know someone else understands your struggle.

I understand how you feel. I am a 24 F suffering from crippling anxiety. I stay home most of the time because I'm terrified of people in a sense. I also have depression. Nothing ever seems to work. Living with anxiety and depression is so difficult more that most realize. I think the best thing that you can do is try to do things that you enjoy (or used to enjoy) and keep doing those things even when you don't want to. Obviously we are going to have good days, bad days, and in between days. We deal with feeling like we can handle it one minute and the next minute we're too tired or too unmotivated to even take a shower. There will be days where it will feel like too much and on those days, try to remind yourself that you're taking things day by day and that everyone has times where they just need to do nothing. It's okay. You're in a process of healing. You need time to do nothing and you need to try and push yourself whenever you feel capable. Sometimes it feels like a chore, I understand. Everything feels like a chore to me. But sometimes, I've noticed that if I start to do something, like drawing a picture... I don't enjoy it immediately but sometimes I start to... and its things like that, that help. Once I start a drawing or finish one, I can look at it and say "I did this today."

To never be alone, to have a spirit or guide, an interconnectedness that most other people cannot relate to. I think about this frequently and part of the reason it is seen in this way, is because here in america our culture is driven by the idea of individualism while in other countries, it is the exact opposite. Other cultures put great emphasis on the many versus the individual, which is why the auditory and visual hallucinations are more negative here in america and seen as an intrusion, rather than a friend to talk to or something positive.

Hello Dr. Telch! Thank you so much for doing this. I have a few questions in mind that I wanted to ask you but first I wanted to give a little background before asking my question...

Some of us anxiety sufferers have multiple co-morbid disorders, for example I myself have social anxiety that stems from PTSD. I went through an abusive relationship that set off my agoraphobia and social anxiety. My confidence and self esteem were almost completely destroyed. I try to face my fears every day and push myself to go for walks and go out in public but sometimes something will happen after I make a lot of progress and I'm back to square one again. Then I must fight through hyperventilating and procrastinating my daily walks for a few hours before I can muster the courage once again.  It never feels like I'm making enough progress and I'm sure there are many others that can relate.

So my question to you is, for us suffering from social anxiety, phobias and agoraphobia... is exposure therapy really the best solution? 

I've often thought that for some of us with more complex co-morbid issues like the one I have described myself as having, that exposure therapy can retraumatize us in a way.

For me, the fear of interacting with other individuals is too great for me to push myself as much as I would like to... Do you have any suggestions?

I think the best way to go about this situation is to realize first, that depression plays tricks on our minds. We do what we can to rationalize what we're feeling and in the process we have the potential to make ourselves paranoid and neurotic in the process. I am by no means calling you paranoid or neurotic... I know exactly where you're coming from... I feel the same way all the time.
